LESSON: READING 10.2.1 NOTE MAKING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Note Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Note Making. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what situations could notes be made?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage
2. value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 10.2.1 NOTE MAKING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 10.2.1 Note Making helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 10.2.1 NOTE MAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage

What this means
In this part you learn to identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.2.1 Note Making”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes

What this means
In this part you learn to value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 10.2.1 Note Making is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.2.1 Note Making”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making to a partner. (skill: value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 10.2.1 Note Making to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage.
3. Practise this skill: value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 10.2.1 Note Making from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 10.2.1 Note Making: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 10.2.1 Note Making?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what situations could notes be made?
2. Why is it important to make notes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 10.2.1 Note Making means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage.
5. Be able to: value the importance of note making while reading for pleasure or academic purposes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
